reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational logic of competitive equilibrium hinges on the principle that productive services adjust continuously until marginal returns equal prices. This leads to a dynamic system where each agent's decision is based on maximizing utility subject to budget constraints. The adjustment mechanism implies a feedback loop between supply and demand, wherein deviations from equilibrium trigger repricing. Theoretically, this process converges towards a stable configuration where no further profitable adjustments exist. However, in practice, friction and bounded rationality prevent such convergence, introducing uncertainty into the model. The dual nature of this system lies in its deterministic evolution under ideal conditions versus stochastic behavior under real-world constraints.
